title: Hansel and Gretel
subtitle: The brother, the sister, and the evil witch.

items.text: Hansel and Gretel
Marcus holds Hofmann's hand all the while.
Tears wet the note, drop by drop.
Causing the ink on it to bleed.
The chaotic thoughts in her mind all recede away. The roaring of her heart begins to slow.
At this moment, only grief and bewilderment remain.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann was calm till the end. Why? Was she not afraid?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No. I just read her fear through her trembling fingers ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But she would not show it. She knew it would've frightened me ...

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Repeat.
The communicator rings again.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: This is the 24 hour countdown to the "Storm." All personnel must return to the headquarters.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Repeat. This is the 24 hour countdown to the "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Beep.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Hofmann, this is Semmelweis. You must leave now. Last call.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: ... You know we won't wait if you miss it.
Marcus turns off the communicator with one hand.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... The "Storm" is coming, doctor.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Come with me to the headquarters. You can take Madam Hofmann's place in the shelter.
The doctor says nothing.
She just lifts her head, gazing up at a non-existent canopy.
Then, she speaks—as if making a plea to the gods above.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: King Midas hunted in the woods, in search of Silenus, the wisest Satyr, the companion of the wine god.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "What is the best and most enticing thing for a man?" The king asked.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The Satyr laughed in response. "Children of mischance and misery! You are asking for an answer you wish not to hear."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "And what is best is beyond your reach: to never be born, to never exist, to be nothing!"

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "But you still have the next best thing: die, and do it soon."
Kakania covers her face, a piercing laugh escaping through her fingertips.
Accompanied shortly after by tears.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I don't care if I could make it through the "Storm."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: My end ... is already upon me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Doctor ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'd rather die here than to spend the rest of my life running from the "Storm."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Get to safety, Ms. Marcus. I still have things to do.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's a shame that we won't get to be colleagues.
She turns resolutely, not once looking back.
But the young apprentice does not stop her.
She is thinking of something more important.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Seeking Silenus in the woods ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Did Theophil write the poem in the same misery and despair?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Then why did he call the painting The Salvation?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: He set fire to every piece of his work, but why leave this one out? And this strange way of drawing ...
Her thoughts are clearer than ever before.
Guilt, madness, blame, a hatred that burns through everything, raging through her thoughts.
The past that once filled that page, it was gone now.
Now no one would make her decisions for her.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Heinrich said he showed the path to salvation and brought "you all" to the Guiding One ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Salvation ... salvation ... Could it be ...
"What really scared me was not the threat to my life, but the possibility of dying ignorant."
She closes her eyes.
All the information she has read in the past, along with the surging blood from the potion, converges before her eyes.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "If I succeed, I can prevent the death of someone who holds the clues."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Even if I die, I'll still turn Kakania completely against Isolde."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This was your plan, madam ...?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "What really scared me was not the threat to my life, but the possibility of dying ignorant."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I know what to do now.
She opens her eyes wide, calling out to the figure as she is about to leave.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Doctor, wait! There might be another way!
But Kakania does not listen. She has made up her mind.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Don't fall into darkness!
The departing figure is held back. Marcus fights with an unprecedented determination.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Don't let madness or despair take over, doctor.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This is not the end. My mission is not over ...!
She reaches into her pocket, silencing the small machine that has been frantically signaling the final evacuation warning.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: There's still another way to end this ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But it can only be done by you and me!
A blaze lights up the street, replacing the glow of dead electric lights.
People fight, throwing themselves into a frenzied hysteria.
The street looks like an exploded powder keg.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: The Guiding One is merciful in bringing this era to an end before the summer of 1914.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Here, the nationalists, the internationalists, the arcanists, the rationalists, the progressives, the conservatives, the fanatics, the bystanders ...

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: They indulge in passion, insisting that it is their ideals that make up the world.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Who would have thought that such a progressive and sensible era would end in a barbaric war?

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Yet in the end, like dust, they will be swept away and forgotten by time.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Only the true believers will survive the end.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: But I must regretfully remind you ...

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Killing one of our own, despite your merits, is a violation of the rules.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: I will report this to the Guiding One.
Her smile remains picture-perfect yet hollow.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: May I have a moment alone, Mr. Forget Me Not?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I want to look at this city one last time.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: ... Whatever you want.
Forget Me Not walks away in boredom.
He has long tired of this maddening conversation.
Isolde stands alone on the street.
People around her celebrate, dance, releasing their inner repression, and their primal passions.
But none of that matters to her.
She is merely waiting.
Waiting for the sky to fall.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... I've thought about this and made up my mind, Isolde.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You were right. I will join you.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I have been waiting to hear this for so, so long ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I know this is what you want. Now, I can finally make your dream come true ...
Kakania extends a handkerchief.
Wiping away her wild-eyed tears of joy.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Before we leave, I would like to take one last walk in this world.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Would you like to join me and walk to my clinic?
TO BE CONTINUED…
